entities.summary: Bacchylides was a Greek lyric poet. Later Greeks included him in the canonical list of Nine Lyric Poets, which included his uncle Simonides. The elegance and polished style of his lyrics have been noted in Bacchylidean scholarship since at least Longinus. Some scholars have characterized these qualities as superficial charm. He has often been compared unfavourably with his contemporary, Pindar, as "a kind of Boccherini to Pindar's Haydn". historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bacchylides' polished style and elegance in his lyrics have had a lasting impact on Greek poetry, influencing later poets such as Longinus. His inclusion in the canonical list of Nine Lyric Poets underscores the significance of his work within the classical Greek literary canon.
